beats.headline: CURSED OCEAN?
beats.short_title: Is the Bermuda Triangle Real? 🔍 Meatball Investigates
beats.comment: Would you sail through it? ⛵ yes / 🚫 no way
beats.bonus: Even the rescue plane sent after Flight 19 was lost, most likely in an explosion. The 'Bermuda Triangle' name comes from a 1964 magazine story by Vincent Gaddis.
beats.caption: Is the Bermuda Triangle cursed? Meatball checked the records. ⛵ or 🚫? #bermudatriangle #mystery #conspiracy #history
sources: NOAA Ocean Service, 'What is the Bermuda Triangle?' (no evidence disappearances happen more often there than in any other large, heavily traveled area of ocean; the US Navy and Coast Guard agree) — https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/bermudatri.html (checked 2026-10-26)
Wikipedia, Flight 19 (5 TBM Avengers lost 5 Dec 1945; navigation error, ran low on fuel over rough seas; PBM Mariner search plane also lost, likely exploded) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_19
Wikipedia, Bermuda Triangle (term from Vincent Gaddis, Argosy, Feb 1964) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_Triangle

beats.headline: FAKE ATTACKS?
beats.short_title: Operation Northwoods: The Conspiracy That Was TRUE 🔍
beats.comment: Did you know this was real? ✅ yes / 😳 no idea
beats.bonus: One idea in the plan: fake the shoot-down of a civilian airliner with a remote-controlled drone. The memo was declassified in 1997.
beats.caption: Operation Northwoods was real: a 1962 plan for fake attacks blamed on Cuba, rejected by Kennedy's team. ✅ or 😳? #conspiracy #history #coldwar #declassified
sources: Joint Chiefs of Staff memorandum 'Justification for US Military Intervention in Cuba', 13 March 1962 (Operation Northwoods), National Security Archive, George Washington University — https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/news/20010430/ (checked 2026-10-26)

Wikipedia, Operation Northwoods (proposed staged attacks incl. a faked shoot-down of a civilian airliner using a drone, blamed on Cuba; rejected by the Kennedy administration; declassified 1997 by the Assassination Records Review Board) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Northwoods

beats.headline: WHAT REALLY CRASHED?
beats.short_title: What REALLY Crashed at Roswell? 🔍 Meatball Investigates
beats.comment: What did you think crashed? 👽 aliens / 🎈 balloon
beats.bonus: Project Mogul's balloons carried microphones to listen for Soviet nuclear tests. The Air Force's reports came out in 1994-1997.
beats.caption: Roswell 1947: the cover-up was real, the aliens weren't. It was Project Mogul. 👽 or 🎈? #roswell #ufo #conspiracy #history
sources: US Air Force, 'The Roswell Report: Fact vs. Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1994/1995) and 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed' (1997): debris came from Project Mogul, a classified balloon train carrying sensors to detect Soviet nuclear tests — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Mogul (checked 2026-10-26)
Wikipedia, Roswell incident (8 July 1947 RAAF press release announced a recovered 'flying disc'; the next day the Army said it was a weather balloon) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roswell_incident

beats.headline: NUKE THE MOON?
beats.short_title: The US Planned to Nuke the Moon. It's REAL 🌕 Meatball Investigates
beats.comment: Would you have pushed the button? 🌕 yes / 🚫 no
beats.bonus: The study, 'A Study of Lunar Research Flights' (AFSWC-TR-59-39, 1959), stayed secret for about 40 years. Carl Sagan worked out how the dust cloud would spread.
beats.caption: In 1958 the US Air Force paid for a study on setting off a nuclear bomb on the Moon. Meatball opened the file. 🌕 or 🚫? #coldwar #weirdhistory #meatballinvestigates #space
sources: Wikipedia, Project A119 (US Air Force project carried out by the Armour Research Foundation at the Illinois Institute of Technology, Chicago, led by Leonard Reiffel; research began May 1958, cancelled January 1959; the blast was meant to be visible from Earth, partly to boost morale after Sputnik; Carl Sagan modelled the expansion of the dust cloud; revealed after Keay Davidson found Sagan had listed classified paper titles in his 1959 application for a Miller Institute fellowship at UC Berkeley) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_A119 (checked 2026-10-26)

L. Reiffel, 'A Study of Lunar Research Flights', Vol. I, Armour Research Foundation for the Air Force Special Weapons Center, 19 June 1959, AFSWC-TR-59-39, DTIC AD0425380 (title page lists C. E. Sagan) — https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/AD0425380.pdf (record checked 2026-10-26)

Keay Davidson, 'Carl Sagan: A Life' (Wiley, 1999); Christopher Chyba, review in Nature (1999); Leonard Reiffel, letter in Nature (2000); Antony Barnett, The Observer, May 2000 (Reiffel confirms the plan)

beats.headline: COULDN'T STOP DANCING?
beats.short_title: The Dancing Plague of 1518 Was REAL 🔍
beats.comment: Could this happen today? 😬 yes / 🙅 no way
beats.bonus: It happened in Strasbourg in July 1518. The physician Paracelsus wrote about it a few years later.
beats.caption: Strasbourg, 1518: people danced for days and the city hired a band to cure it. 😬 or 🙅? #dancingplague #history #weirdhistory #mystery
sources: Wikipedia, Dancing plague of 1518 (Strasbourg, July 1518; began with one woman, Frau Troffea; dozens joined within a week; authorities prescribed more dancing, built a stage and hired musicians; leading explanation mass psychogenic illness amid famine and disease, ergot theory disputed) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_plague_of_1518 (checked 2026-10-26)
John Waller, 'A forgotten plague: making sense of dancing mania', The Lancet 373 (2009): 624-625 — https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(09)60386-X
